allHealthy.title: All healthy
allHealthy.detail: Nothing unusual found — the tunnel configuration and its connection look normal.
suggestions: If the tunnel is still not working, try stopping and starting it again
Check the run logs for occasional errors

tokenMismatch.title: Token mismatch
tokenMismatch.detail: The token carried by the local frpc does not match the one configured in frps on the server, so the server rejected the connection.
suggestions: Run “Deploy / Upgrade” for this server on the Servers page to regenerate the token, then start the tunnel again
If you edited the server config manually, make sure the token in frpc matches the token in the server's frps config exactly

authFailed.title: SSH authentication failed
authFailed.detail: The server rejected the credentials used to connect.
suggestions: Double-check the username and the password / key path
When logging in with a key, make sure its public key is in the server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
Run ssh user@host in a terminal to verify you can log in

versionMismatch.title: frpc / frps version mismatch
versionMismatch.detail: The client and server frp versions differ too much, which can break protocol compatibility.
suggestions: Run “Deploy / Upgrade” for this server to update frps to a matching version
Reinstall the frpc engine under Settings → Engines so both ends match

portConflict.title: Port already in use
portConflict.detail: A port frps needs to listen on is occupied by another process on the server.
suggestions: Log in to the server and run ss -tlnp | grep <port> to find the process holding the port
Change the frps ports in the advanced options when adding the server, then deploy again
If an old frps is left over, run “Uninstall” and then “Deploy” to clean it up

connectionRefused.title: Connection refused
connectionRefused.detail: Nothing is listening on the target port, or a firewall is blocking it.
suggestions: Check that the server firewall / cloud security group allows TCP 7000 (the frp bind port)
Make sure frps is running on the server: run “Deploy / Upgrade” or “Test connection”
Verify the server address and port used by the tunnel are correct

connectionTimeout.title: Connection timed out
connectionTimeout.detail: Establishing a connection to the server timed out — network unreachable, firewall dropping packets, or the server is offline.
suggestions: Make sure the server is online and reachable: ping <server address>
Check that the server firewall / cloud security group allows TCP 7000 (the frp bind port)
Pier will retry automatically; cross-border routes may need another moment

dnsFailed.title: DNS lookup failed
dnsFailed.detail: The server address or subdomain could not be resolved to an IP.
suggestions: Run nslookup <domain> in a terminal to see what it resolves to
Check that the server's A record points to the correct public IP
For self-hosted servers, make sure the wildcard *.subdomainHost resolves to the server

localServiceDown.title: Local service unreachable
localServiceDown.detail: Nothing is listening on the local address this tunnel forwards to.
suggestions: Make sure the local service is running; verify with curl http://127.0.0.1:<port>
Check that the tunnel's local host and port are correct
If the service binds to a specific interface only, try 127.0.0.1 as the local host

binaryMissing.title: Tunnel engine not installed
binaryMissing.detail: The engine required by this tunnel (cloudflared / bore / frpc) is missing on this machine.
suggestions: Pier usually downloads missing engines automatically at start — check your network and retry
You can also install the engine manually in “Settings → Engines”
Restart the tunnel once the engine is installed

remoteServerUnreachable.title: Server unreachable
remoteServerUnreachable.detail: A network connection to the server could not be established.
suggestions: Verify the server IP / hostname and SSH port
Check that the server firewall / cloud security group allows your SSH port (default 22)
Run ping <server address> in a terminal to test connectivity

genericError.title: Tunnel problem
genericError.detail: The tunnel hit a problem that could not be classified automatically.
suggestions: Check the run logs for the detailed error
Stop and start the tunnel again
If it keeps happening, run “Deploy / Upgrade” for the server again

help.title: Help Center
help.subtitle: Guide to fixed hostnames (Cloudflare Named Tunnel)
help.modeTempDesc: No account needed — works instantly. The hostname changes every start; great for quick demos and debugging.
help.modeFixedDesc: Bind your Cloudflare account and domain — the subdomain stays fixed across reconnects, restarts and new machines.
help.getTokenTitle: Get a Cloudflare API Token (3 steps)
help.getTokenSubtitle: You only do this once; the token is stored in your OS keychain and never uploaded.
help.step1Title: Open the Cloudflare tokens page and create a custom token
help.step1Body: Sign in to Cloudflare, go to “My Profile → API Tokens”, click “Create Token → Create Custom Token → Get started”.
help.step2Body: First row: Account / Cloudflare Tunnel / Edit. Add two more rows: Zone / DNS / Edit and Zone / Zone / Read. Zone Resources: Include → All zones.
help.step3Title: Continue to summary, then create and copy
help.step3Body: Click “Continue to summary”, confirm, create the token and copy the value (shown only once), then paste it into the ShengShouMaTou new-tunnel wizard.
help.permFooter: Tip: you can Roll the token anytime in the Cloudflare dashboard — existing tunnels keep working.
help.faq1Q: What does a fixed hostname require?
help.faq1A: A domain with its NS hosted on Cloudflare (bought anywhere; hosting is free). The free plan includes fixed hostnames.
help.faq2A: Usually a missing permission: make sure the three levels are Edit / Edit / Read and the zone resources include your domain. Fix it and retry — no need to recreate the token.
help.faq3Q: It says the subdomain is taken?
help.faq3A: A DNS record for that subdomain already exists and points elsewhere. Pick another subdomain, or delete the old record in the Cloudflare dashboard first.
help.faq4A: Cloudflare tunnels need outbound access to port 7844 (QUIC/HTTP2). Some networks block UDP; the app already defaults to the more compatible HTTP2 protocol.
help.faq5Q: Does closing the window quit the app?
help.faq5A: No. Closing the window minimizes the app to the system tray and tunnels keep running; to quit completely, use “Quit” in the tray menu.

update.autoCheckHint: The app checks for updates on startup and then every hour. You can also check manually anytime.
